title: Optical Control of Actin Network Assembly on the Supported Lipid Bilayer
author: Kei Yamamoto
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Actin (10% labeled with Alexa Fluor 647) (see [30,31] for the purification method)

Capping protein (CP) (see [30] for the purification method) Note: Plasmids required for protein expression are available from the authors upon request. Plasmids used for the expression of His-mEGFP-iLID and SspB-mScarlet-I-VCA will be deposited at Addgene. Reagents
18:1 DGS-NTA(Ni) [DGS-NTA(Ni)] (Avanti, catalog number: 790404); product format: 10 mg/mL in chloroform
16:0–18:1 PC (POPC) (Avanti, catalog number: 850457); product format: powder
Riboflavin 5′-monophosphate sodium salt hydrate (FMN) (Sigma, catalog number: F
Creatine phosphokinase from rabbit muscle (CPK) (Sigma, catalog number: C
Phosphocreatine disodium salt hydrate (Pcr) (Sigma, catalog number: P
Adenosine 5’-triphosphate disodium salt n-hydrate (ATP) (Wako, catalog number: 019-

steps.title: Make 1× PBS pH 6.5
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8 g NaCl, 0.2 g KCl, 1.15 g Na₂HPO₄, and 0.2 g KH₂PO₄ in Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 6.5 with HCl, and bring the final volume to 1 L.

steps.title: Make glass washing solution
steps.instruction: Mix 800 mL 100 % ethanol with 50 g NaOH (50 g L⁻¹) and bring the volume to 1 L with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Make 10× A50 buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 500 mL 1 M HEPES‑KOH (pH 7.6), 250 mL 2 M KCl, 50 mL 1 M MgCl₂, and 50 mL 0.2 M EGTA, then bring to 1 L with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare SspB mixture (20 µL)
steps.instruction: In 20 µL total volume mix 2 µL 20 mM Trolox in A50 buffer, 1 µL 200 µM FMN in A50 buffer, 0.7 µL 4.3 µM SspB‑mScarlet‑I‑VCA in A50 buffer, and 16.3 µL 1× A50 buffer.

steps.title: Prepare 20× energy mix (10 µL)
steps.instruction: Combine 1 µL 0.2 M ATP in A50 buffer, 5 µL 0.4 M phosphocreatine (Pcr) in A50 buffer, 2 µL 10 mg mL⁻¹ creatine phosphokinase (CPK) in A50 buffer, and 2 µL 1 M DTT in A50 buffer; mix fresh before each experiment.

steps.title: Prepare polymerization mixture (20 µL)
steps.instruction: On ice, add 2 µL 2× A50 buffer, 2 µL 20 mM Trolox in A50 buffer, 1 µL 20× energy mix, 1 µL 200 µM FMN in A50 buffer, 1.5 µL 200 µM profilin in A50 buffer, 2 µL 250 nM capping protein (CP) in A50 buffer, 0.7 µL 2.8 µM Arp2/3 complex in A50 buffer, 0.7 µL 4.3 µM SspB‑mScarlet‑I‑VCA in A50 buffer, 2 µL 50 µM actin in G‑buffer, and 7.1 µL 1× A50 buffer; keep all solutions on ice, add actin last, mix within 5 min and load immediately into a flow cell.

steps.title: Prepare vesicle stock solution
steps.instruction: Follow the substeps to generate a 1 mM DGS‑NTA(Ni)/POPC vesicle stock.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 132.15 µL of 10 mg mL⁻¹ (9.46 mM) DGS‑NTA(Ni) in chloroform into glass tubes.
Dry tubes overnight in a vacuum desiccator.
Fill glove bag with nitrogen and cap dried DGS‑NTA(Ni) tubes under nitrogen.
Aliquot 5–10 mg POPC powder into Eppendorf tubes under nitrogen (determine mass by weight difference).
Vacuum‑seal both DGS‑NTA(Ni) and POPC tubes and store frozen until use (≈6 months usable).
Add 62.5 µL chloroform to DGS‑NTA(Ni) tube to make a 20 mM solution.
Add chloroform to POPC tube to make a 20 mM solution (volume adjusted to powder amount).
In a new glass tube mix 7.2 µL DGS‑NTA(Ni) with 112.8 µL POPC to obtain 6 % (mol/mol) DGS‑NTA(Ni) in POPC.
Aliquot 50 µL of this mixture into two new glass tubes.
Dry the tubes overnight in a vacuum desiccator.
Add 1 mL PBS (pH 6.5) to each tube, vortex 30 s, cap, and store at 4 °C overnight.
Transfer vesicle suspension to an Eppendorf tube, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, thaw in a 30 °C water bath, and repeat freeze‑thaw cycle five times to obtain unilamellar vesicles.
Aliquot the resulting solution and store at –80 °C as a 1 mM stock (≈3 months usable).

steps.title: Optimize light illumination intensity
steps.instruction: Determine suitable blue‑light power for iLID activation using the microscope and DMD.

substeps.instruction: Start computer, microscope, and launch NIS‑Elements; set excitation lasers (405, 488, 561, 640 nm) and filters as described, and configure DMD filters (DM 500 nm, excitation 470/40 nm, emission 535/50 nm).
Insert a neutral‑density (ND) filter into the DMD output path (iLID activates at 1–5 % software output).
Darken the room, place a power sensor on the objective, and calibrate the DMD light path per manufacturer’s protocol.
Define a region of interest (ROI) in NIS‑Elements, illuminate with blue light, and record the intensity; generate a calibration curve covering 0.04–0.18 nW µm⁻².

steps.title: Assemble handmade flow cell
steps.instruction: Construct a flow chamber of ~10–15 µL volume using coverslips, double‑sided tape, and VaLaP.

substeps.instruction: Place 24 × 60 mm coverslips in a stainless rack, immerse in glass‑washing solution, and sonicate for 90 min.
Rinse coverslips and rack five times with Milli‑Q water, then wash in Milli‑Q water for 60 min and rinse again five times.
Confirm coverslip surfaces are hydrophilic; store in water‑filled rack for up to two weeks.
Dry coverslips with nitrogen gas, then plasma‑clean for ~5 min.
Apply two strips of double‑sided tape (0.3 mm thick) on the plasma‑treated coverslip leaving a 2–3 mm gap, and place an 18 × 18 mm coverslip on top to form the channel.
Melt VaLaP on a hot plate and brush it to seal all channel areas except inlet and outlet; the assembled flow cell can be stored in air for 2–3 days.

steps.title: Form iLID‑bound lipid bilayer
steps.instruction: Create a supported lipid bilayer with His‑mEGFP‑iLID in a dark (red‑light) environment.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the 1 mM vesicle stock threefold with PBS (pH 6.5) to obtain 0.33 mM vesicles; adjust volume based on flow‑cell dimensions.
Assemble a mini‑extruder with membrane filter and filter support.
Pass the vesicle solution through a syringe 10 times to homogenize size.
Inject 20 µL vesicle solution into the flow cell, incubate at room temperature for 10 min in a humidity chamber (wet filter paper, Parafilm cover) to prevent drying.
Wash out excess vesicles with 50 µL 1× A50 buffer, dispensing at the inlet while absorbing at the outlet with filter paper; avoid bubbles.
Add 20 µL His‑mEGFP‑iLID (7 µM final) to the flow cell, incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Secure the flow cell on the microscope stage with VaLaP and double‑sided tape.
Wash out unbound His‑mEGFP‑iLID with 50 µL 1× A50 buffer.
Inspect the membrane under the microscope; image central region to avoid edge heterogeneity.

steps.title: Induce actin polymerization with light
steps.instruction: Trigger actin network assembly on the iLID‑coated bilayer using patterned blue illumination.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the polymerization mixture on ice (see step “Prepare polymerization mixture”).
Load the mixture into the flow cell on the microscope stage and seal inlet/outlet with VaLaP.
Focus on the SspB‑mScarlet‑I‑VCA signal, enable perfect focus, and set up imaging.

Run the experiment: illuminate the ROI with 500 ms blue light every 20 s (using NIS‑Elements JOBS), acquire images; SspB recruitment appears ~20 s after illumination, followed by actin polymerization.
